claim: Skeletal muscle myoblasts (iMyoblasts) were generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) using an efficient and reliable transgene-free induction and stem cell selection protocol.
source: Skeletal muscle myoblasts (iMyoblasts) were generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) using an efficient and reliable transgene-free induction and stem cell selection protocol.
evidence: The abstract directly states the method used to generate iMyoblasts from iPSCs.

claim: iMyoblasts are identified as a PAX3+/MYOD1+ skeletal myogenic lineage with a fetal-like transcriptome signature.
source: Immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, qPCR, digital RNA expression profiling, and scRNA-Seq studies identify iMyoblasts as a PAX3+/MYOD1+ skeletal myogenic lineage with a fetal-like transcriptome signature, distinct from adult muscle biopsy myoblasts (bMyoblasts) and iPSC-induced muscle progenitors.
evidence: Multiple experimental techniques (immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, qPCR, digital RNA expression profiling, and scRNA-Seq) were used to characterize iMyoblasts.

claim: iMyoblasts are distinct from adult muscle biopsy myoblasts (bMyoblasts) and iPSC-induced muscle progenitors.
source: Immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, qPCR, digital RNA expression profiling, and scRNA-Seq studies identify iMyoblasts as a PAX3+/MYOD1+ skeletal myogenic lineage with a fetal-like transcriptome signature, distinct from adult muscle biopsy myoblasts (bMyoblasts) and iPSC-induced muscle progenitors.
evidence: Comparative analysis using multiple techniques showed differences between iMyoblasts and other myogenic cell types.

claim: iMyoblasts can be stably propagated for >12 passages or 30 population doublings while retaining their dual commitment for myotube differentiation and regeneration of reserve cells.
source: iMyoblasts can be stably propagated for >12 passages or 30 population doublings while retaining their dual commitment for myotube differentiation and regeneration of reserve cells.
evidence: The abstract states the expansion capacity and functional characteristics of iMyoblasts.

claim: iMyoblasts efficiently xenoengrafted into irradiated and injured mouse muscle where they undergo differentiation and fetal-adult MYH isoform switching.
source: iMyoblasts also efficiently xenoengrafted into irradiated and injured mouse muscle where they undergo differentiation and fetal-adult MYH isoform switching, demonstrating their regulatory plasticity for adult muscle maturation in response to signals in the host muscle.
evidence: In vivo xenograft experiments demonstrated iMyoblast engraftment and differentiation.

claim: iMyoblasts demonstrate regulatory plasticity for adult muscle maturation in response to signals in the host muscle.
source: iMyoblasts also efficiently xenoengrafted into irradiated and injured mouse muscle where they undergo differentiation and fetal-adult MYH isoform switching, demonstrating their regulatory plasticity for adult muscle maturation in response to signals in the host muscle.
evidence: The observation of MYH isoform switching in xenografts indicates plasticity in response to host signals.

claim: Xenograft muscle retains PAX3+ muscle progenitors and can regenerate human muscle in response to secondary injury.
source: Xenograft muscle retains PAX3+ muscle progenitors and can regenerate human muscle in response to secondary injury.
evidence: Secondary injury experiments demonstrated the regenerative capacity of xenografted muscle.

claim: iMyoblasts from individuals with Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy revealed a previously unknown epigenetic regulatory mechanism controlling developmental expression of the pathological DUX4 gene.
source: As models of disease, iMyoblasts from individuals with Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy revealed a previously unknown epigenetic regulatory mechanism controlling developmental expression of the pathological DUX4 gene.
evidence: Disease modeling experiments with FSHD iMyoblasts revealed novel epigenetic regulation of DUX4.

claim: iMyoblasts from Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy R7 and R9 and Walker Warburg Syndrome patients modeled their molecular disease pathologies.
source: iMyoblasts from Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy R7 and R9 and Walker Warburg Syndrome patients modeled their molecular disease pathologies and were responsive to small molecule and gene editing therapeutics.
evidence: Disease modeling experiments demonstrated that iMyoblasts recapitulate disease pathologies.

claim: iMyoblasts from LGMDR7, LGMDR9, and WWS patients were responsive to small molecule and gene editing therapeutics.
source: iMyoblasts from Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy R7 and R9 and Walker Warburg Syndrome patients modeled their molecular disease pathologies and were responsive to small molecule and gene editing therapeutics.
evidence: Therapeutic intervention experiments showed responsiveness to treatments.

claim: Technologies for reprogramming human somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were reported by Takahashi et al., 2007.
source: The technologies for reprogramming human somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) (Takahashi et al., 2007) and for inducing specific differentiated cell types are providing extraordinary opportunities for investigating mechanisms of human tissue differentiation, the molecular pathology of diseases, and therapeutic development.
evidence: Citation to Takahashi et al., 2007 supports the claim about iPSC technology.

claim: Less attention has been given to generation of lineage-specific human stem cells and progenitors compared to differentiated cells.
source: Much of the research on iPS cell-type induction has focused on optimizing the production of differentiated cells to provide a platform for investigations of disease pathologies (Ardhanareeswaran et al., 2017; Hashimoto et al., 2016; Georgomanoli and Papapetrou, 2019; Heslop and Duncan, 2019; van Mil et al., 2018). Less attention has been given to generation of lineage-specific human stem cells and progenitors to enable studies of tissue and organ development, genetic and epigenetic disease mechanisms, and stem cell therapeutics.
evidence: The text contrasts the focus on differentiated cells versus progenitor cells in the field.

claim: The goal of the study was to isolate and propagate myogenic stem cells from human iPSC cultures in response to gene-free myogenic induction and cell growth selection.
source: The goal of our study has been to isolate and propagate myogenic stem cells from human iPSC cultures in response to gene-free myogenic induction and cell growth selection and to establish the utility of these myoblast stem cells for molecular investigations of human myogenesis and muscular dystrophies.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the study's goal.

claim: The protocol efficiently produces a stably committed and expandable population of PAX3+/MYOD1+ iMyoblasts.
source: This protocol efficiently produces a stably committed and expandable population of PAX3+/MYOD1+ iMyoblasts that differentiate as regenerative stem cells ex vivo in cell culture and in vivo in muscle xenografts in irradiated and injured mouse tibialis anterior (TA) muscle, which maintain a renewable PAX3+ iMyoblast population.
evidence: The introduction describes the characteristics of iMyoblasts produced by the protocol.

claim: iMyoblasts differentiate as regenerative stem cells ex vivo in cell culture and in vivo in muscle xenografts.
source: This protocol efficiently produces a stably committed and expandable population of PAX3+/MYOD1+ iMyoblasts that differentiate as regenerative stem cells ex vivo in cell culture and in vivo in muscle xenografts in irradiated and injured mouse tibialis anterior (TA) muscle, which maintain a renewable PAX3+ iMyoblast population.
evidence: The introduction describes the differentiation capacity of iMyoblasts in different contexts.

claim: iMyoblast muscle xenografts undergo fetal-to-adult MYH isoform switching.
source: iMyoblast muscle xenografts undergo fetal-to-adult MYH isoform switching demonstrating their plasticity to respond to maturation signals provided by the host adult muscle.
evidence: The introduction states the observation of MYH isoform switching in xenografts.

claim: iMyoblasts generated from FSHD1, LGMDR7, LGMDR9, and WWS patient iPSCs model the molecular pathologies of these diseases.
source: Finally, we show that iMyoblasts generated from Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy (FSHD) Type 1 (FSHD1), Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy (LGMD) R7 and R9 (formerly LGMD2G and 2I), and Walker Warburg Syndrome (WWS) patient iPSCs model the molecular pathologies of these diseases.
evidence: The introduction states that disease iMyoblasts model disease pathologies.

claim: A two-step protocol was developed to isolate iMyoblasts from cultures of Ctrl and patient iPSCs, using transgene-free iPSC myogenic induction in combination with reserve cell selection.
source: We developed a two-step protocol to isolate iMyoblasts from cultures of Ctrl and patient iPSCs, using transgene-free iPSC myogenic induction in combination with reserve cell selection (Figure 1A).
evidence: The Results section describes the protocol development and Figure 1A illustrates it.

claim: Human iPSC lines for these studies were generated by reprogramming bMyoblasts and fibroblasts isolated from muscle biopsies of adult FSHD1 and Ctrl subjects.
source: Human iPSC lines for these studies were generated by reprogramming bMyoblasts and fibroblasts isolated from muscle biopsies of adult FSHD1 and Ctrl subjects (Homma et al., 2012; Jones et al., 2012), or dermal fibroblasts from subjects with early onset FSHD1, LGMDR7, LGMDR9, and WWS (Kava et al., 2013).
evidence: The Results section describes the source of iPSC lines with citations.

claim: The first step of the iMyoblast protocol was transgene-free iPSC myogenesis induction using commercially available reagents.
source: The first step of the iMyoblast protocol was transgene-free iPSC myogenesis induction using commercially available reagents (Caron et al., 2016; Amsbio, Skeletal Muscle differentiation Kit) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The Results section describes the first step of the protocol with citation and figure reference.

claim: The three-stage iPSC myogenesis protocol induces cultures of Ctrl and disease iPSCs to sequentially upregulate expression of muscle master regulators, PAX3 (S1 stage) and MYOD1 (S2 stage), and the muscle differentiation marker MYH8 (S3 Stage).
source: This three-stage iPSC myogenesis protocol induces cultures of Ctrl and disease iPSCs to sequentially upregulate expression of muscle master regulators, PAX3 (S1 stage) and MYOD1 (S2 stage), and the muscle differentiation marker MYH8 (S3 Stage) (Caron et al., 2016), as assayed by qPCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The Results section describes the sequential upregulation of markers with qPCR data shown in a figure.

claim: Ctrl and disease iPSC and ESC lines robustly upregulated expression of PAX3, MYOD1, and MYH8 on the order of 1000-fold during S1, S2, and S3 stages of myogenic induction.
source: These studies established that Ctrl and disease iPSC and ESC lines robustly upregulated expression of PAX3, MYOD1, and MYH8 on the order of 1000-fold during S1, S2, and S3 stages of myogenic induction, validating the consistency and efficiency of the transgene-free induction protocol.
evidence: The Results section quantifies the upregulation of markers during induction.

claim: 90% of cells in S2 stage cultures were MYOD1+.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) assays showed that 90% of cells in S2 stage cultures were MYOD1+, and 80% of cells in S3 stage cultures were MF20+ and predominantly mononucleated iMyocytes (Figure 1A), similar to the first myogenic cells to differentiate in the embryo (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: Immunofluorescence assays quantified the percentage of MYOD1+ cells in S2 cultures.

claim: 80% of cells in S3 stage cultures were MF20+ and predominantly mononucleated iMyocytes.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) assays showed that 90% of cells in S2 stage cultures were MYOD1+, and 80% of cells in S3 stage cultures were MF20+ and predominantly mononucleated iMyocytes (Figure 1A), similar to the first myogenic cells to differentiate in the embryo (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: Immunofluorescence assays quantified the percentage of MF20+ cells in S3 cultures.

claim: S3 stage iMyocytes are similar to the first myogenic cells to differentiate in the embryo.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) assays showed that 90% of cells in S2 stage cultures were MYOD1+, and 80% of cells in S3 stage cultures were MF20+ and predominantly mononucleated iMyocytes (Figure 1A), similar to the first myogenic cells to differentiate in the embryo (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: The Results section compares S3 iMyocytes to embryonic myogenic cells with citation.

claim: PAX7 expression was detected at 100-fold lower levels than PAX3 during S1 induction.
source: PAX7 expression was detected at 100-fold lower levels than PAX3 during S1 induction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), consistent with earlier findings that PAX7+ cells are a minor cell population induced by transgene-free myogenesis protocols (Chal et al., 2015; van der Wal et al., 2018).
evidence: qPCR data showed lower PAX7 expression compared to PAX3.

claim: PAX7+ cells are a minor cell population induced by transgene-free myogenesis protocols.
source: PAX7 expression was detected at 100-fold lower levels than PAX3 during S1 induction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), consistent with earlier findings that PAX7+ cells are a minor cell population induced by transgene-free myogenesis protocols (Chal et al., 2015; van der Wal et al., 2018).
evidence: The Results section cites earlier findings about PAX7+ cells in transgene-free protocols.

claim: bMyoblasts and iMyoblasts expressed muscle master regulatory genes PAX3 and MYOD1 in growth factor-rich medium.
source: In growth factor-rich medium, bMyoblasts and iMyoblasts expressed muscle master regulatory genes PAX3 and MYOD1 whereas adult bMyoblasts expressed PAX7 in addition to PAX3 and MYOD1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: qPCR data showed expression of PAX3 and MYOD1 in both cell types.

claim: Adult bMyoblasts expressed PAX7 in addition to PAX3 and MYOD1.
source: In growth factor-rich medium, bMyoblasts and iMyoblasts expressed muscle master regulatory genes PAX3 and MYOD1 whereas adult bMyoblasts expressed PAX7 in addition to PAX3 and MYOD1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: qPCR data showed expression of PAX7, PAX3, and MYOD1 in adult bMyoblasts.

claim: iMyoblasts proliferated in myoblast growth medium with 12 hr cell doubling times.
source: iMyoblasts proliferated in myoblast growth medium with 12 hr cell doubling times and could be expanded as primary lines for more than 12 passages (>30 population doublings) while cell-autonomously maintaining expression of PAX3 and MYOD1 and the commitment to differentiate in response to growth factor free medium, as assayed by expression of MYH8 and CKM (Figure 1C).
evidence: The Results section states the cell doubling time for iMyoblasts.

claim: iMyoblasts could be expanded as primary lines for more than 12 passages (>30 population doublings) while cell-autonomously maintaining expression of PAX3 and MYOD1 and the commitment to differentiate.
source: iMyoblasts proliferated in myoblast growth medium with 12 hr cell doubling times and could be expanded as primary lines for more than 12 passages (>30 population doublings) while cell-autonomously maintaining expression of PAX3 and MYOD1 and the commitment to differentiate in response to growth factor free medium, as assayed by expression of MYH8 and CKM (Figure 1C).
evidence: The Results section describes the expansion capacity and maintenance of myogenic markers in iMyoblasts.

claim: During their differentiation, iMyoblasts fused to form multinucleated iMyotubes.
source: During their differentiation, iMyoblasts fused to form multinucleated iMyotubes (Figure 1A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showed multinucleated iMyotubes.

claim: Proliferating FSHD1 and Ctrl iMyoblasts expressed cell surface markers typical of fetal and adult myogenic cells, including CD82, CD56, CD318, ERBB3, and NGFR.
source: Proliferating FSHD1 and Ctrl iMyoblasts expressed cell surface markers typical of fetal and adult myogenic cells, including CD82 (Alexander et al., 2016; Pakula et al., 2019) as well as CD56, CD318 (Uezumi et al., 2016), ERBB3, and NGFR (Hicks et al., 2018; Figure 1D).
evidence: Flow cytometry data showed expression of multiple cell surface markers.

claim: FAC-sorted CD82+/CD56+ and CD82+/CD56− iMyoblasts both differentiated and fused to form MF20+ iMyotubes.
source: FAC-sorted CD82+/CD56+ and CD82+/CD56− iMyoblasts both differentiated and fused to form MF20+ iMyotubes, validating the commitment of CD82+ iMyoblasts to differentiate (Figure 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence of sorted cells showed differentiation capacity.

claim: iMyoblasts retained their dual commitment to both differentiate and generate reserve cells that could be recovered by growth medium stimulation as MYOD1+ iMyoblasts (tMyoblasts) that can fuse and differentiate as MF20+ and MEF2C + iMyotubes.
source: Finally, iMyoblasts retained their dual commitment to both differentiate and generate reserve cells that could be recovered by growth medium stimulation as MYOD1+ iMyoblasts (tMyoblasts) that can fuse and differentiate as MF20+ and MEF2C + iMyotubes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Reserve cell selection experiments showed the dual commitment of iMyoblasts.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) was used to define the iMyoblast transcriptome and compare it to transcriptome signatures of adult muscle bMyoblasts, and S1 and S2 stage cells undergoing iPSC myogenic induction.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) was used to define the iMyoblast transcriptome and compare it to transcriptome signatures of adult muscle bMyoblasts, and S1 and S2 stage cells undergoing iPSC myogenic induction.
evidence: The Results section describes the use of scRNA-Seq for transcriptome analysis.

claim: iMyoblasts were generated by iPSC induction and reserve cell propagation from S3 cultures from iPSCs reprogrammed from parental CD56+ muscle biopsy cells of six subjects, including two classic FSHD1 subjects (15A and 30A), one early onset FSHD1 subject (17A), and their unaffected Ctrl family members (15V, 17U, and 30W).
source: For these studies, iMyoblasts were generated by iPSC induction and reserve cell propagation from S3 cultures. iPSCs were reprogrammed from parental CD56+ muscle biopsy cells of six subjects, including two classic FSHD1 subjects (15A and 30A), one early onset FSHD1 subject (17A), and their unaffected Ctrl family members (15V, 17U, and 30W).
evidence: The Results section describes the source of cells for scRNA-Seq analysis.

claim: The UMAP plots grouped Ctrl and FSHD1 cells together in each of the five main clusters.
source: The Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) plots grouped Ctrl and FSHD1 cells together in each of the five main clusters (Figure 2B), as expected as the FSHD1 disease genes are expressed in differentiated myotubes and not in proliferating progenitors.
evidence: UMAP analysis showed clustering of cells by type rather than disease status.

claim: FSHD1 disease genes are expressed in differentiated myotubes and not in proliferating progenitors.
source: The Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) plots grouped Ctrl and FSHD1 cells together in each of the five main clusters (Figure 2B), as expected as the FSHD1 disease genes are expressed in differentiated myotubes and not in proliferating progenitors.
evidence: The Results section explains why FSHD1 and Ctrl cells cluster together.

claim: UMAP grouped Ctrl and FSHD iMyoblasts into clusters that were distinct from S1, S2, bMyoblast (bMyo), and biopsy mesodermal cell (bMes) clusters.
source: UMAP grouped Ctrl and FSHD iMyoblasts into clusters that were distinct from S1, S2, bMyoblast (bMyo), and biopsy mesodermal cell (bMes) clusters.
evidence: UMAP analysis showed distinct clustering of iMyoblasts.

claim: Each cell type cluster included subsets of cells expressing genes of the different stages of the cell cycle and cells contributed by all six subjects.
source: Each cell type cluster included subsets of cells expressing genes of the different stages of the cell cycle and cells contributed by all six subjects, consistent with a reliable and sensitive UMAP segregation (Figure 2B).
evidence: UMAP analysis showed distribution of cell cycle stages and subjects across clusters.

claim: Each of the five clusters had a distinct gene expression signature of myogenic regulatory genes, differentiation genes, and cluster marker genes that further validated their myogenic identities.
source: Each of the five clusters had a distinct gene expression signature of myogenic regulatory genes, differentiation genes, and cluster marker genes that further validated their myogenic identities (Figure 2C).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed distinct signatures for each cluster.

claim: The iMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1.
source: The iMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1, the bMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1 as well as PAX7 and MYF5, and the bMes non-myogenic cluster expressed PDGFRA, a mesodermal cell marker (Evseenko et al., 2010; Joe et al., 2010; Uezumi et al., 2010; Ding et al., 2013).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed PAX3 and MYOD1 expression in iMyoblasts.

claim: The bMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1 as well as PAX7 and MYF5.
source: The iMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1, the bMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1 as well as PAX7 and MYF5, and the bMes non-myogenic cluster expressed PDGFRA, a mesodermal cell marker (Evseenko et al., 2010; Joe et al., 2010; Uezumi et al., 2010; Ding et al., 2013).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed expression of multiple myogenic markers in bMyoblasts.

claim: The bMes non-myogenic cluster expressed PDGFRA, a mesodermal cell marker.
source: The iMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1, the bMyoblast cluster expressed PAX3 and MYOD1 as well as PAX7 and MYF5, and the bMes non-myogenic cluster expressed PDGFRA, a mesodermal cell marker (Evseenko et al., 2010; Joe et al., 2010; Uezumi et al., 2010; Ding et al., 2013).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed PDGFRA expression in bMes cells with citations.

claim: bMyo and bMes cells expressed NFIX, a regulator of the switch from embryonic to fetal myogenesis.
source: bMyo and bMes cells expressed NFIX, a regulator of the switch from embryonic to fetal myogenesis (Messina et al., 2010), also expressed by iMyoblasts at lower levels (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed NFIX expression with citation.

claim: iMyoblasts expressed NFIX at lower levels than bMyo and bMes cells.
source: bMyo and bMes cells expressed NFIX, a regulator of the switch from embryonic to fetal myogenesis (Messina et al., 2010), also expressed by iMyoblasts at lower levels (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed lower NFIX expression in iMyoblasts.

claim: Cells in the S1 cluster expressed PAX3 at higher levels than cells in the iMyoblast cluster and expressed LIN28A, which encodes an RNA binding protein controlling self-renewal and differentiation.
source: Cells in the S1 cluster expressed PAX3 at higher levels than cells in the iMyoblast cluster and expressed LIN28A, which encodes an RNA binding protein controlling self-renewal and differentiation (Shyh-Chang and Daley, 2013).
evidence: Gene expression analysis showed higher PAX3 and LIN28A expression in S1 cells with citation.

claim: S2 cells had heterogeneous morphology and could be subdivided into a proximal S2A subcluster expressing PAX3 and a more distal S2B subcluster expressing MYOD1, MYOG, and MYH8 muscle differentiation genes, and G1 cell cycle markers.
source: S2 cells had heterogeneous morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and could be subdivided into a proximal S2A subcluster expressing PAX3 and a more distal S2B subcluster expressing MYOD1, MYOG, and MYH8 muscle differentiation genes, and G1 cell cycle markers, consistent with their developmental progression from pre- to post-differentiation stages.
evidence: Gene expression and morphology analysis showed heterogeneity in S2 cells.

claim: These findings establish iMyoblasts as a myogenic cell with a transcriptome distinct from bMyoblasts and S1 and S2 stage myogenic cells.
source: These findings establish iMyoblasts as a myogenic cell with a transcriptome distinct from bMyoblasts and S1 and S2 stage myogenic cells.
evidence: The Results section summarizes the scRNA-Seq findings.

claim: Differences in gene expression between iMyoblasts, bMyoblasts, bMes, S1, S2A, and S2B cell classes were quantitated and subjected to pathway analysis using edgeR.
source: Differences in gene expression between iMyoblasts, bMyoblasts, bMes, S1, S2A, and S2B cell classes were quantitated and subjected to pathway analysis using edgeR (Robinson et al., 2010).
evidence: The Results section describes the pathway analysis method with citation.

claim: The 15 pairwise comparisons among the six cell classes each identified at least 4600 differentially expressed coding and non-coding genes at a false discovery rate (FDR)<0.05.
source: The 15 pairwise comparisons among the six cell classes each identified at least 4600 differentially expressed coding and non-coding genes at a false discovery rate (FDR)<0.05 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Differential expression analysis identified thousands of differentially expressed genes.

claim: The top-ranked categories for the iMyoblast versus bMyoblast comparison included categories of known myogenic genes, including ECM, focal adhesion, and migration/chemotaxis.
source: The top-ranked categories for the iMyoblast versus bMyoblast comparison included categories of known myogenic genes, including ECM, focal adhesion, and migration/chemotaxis (Gillies and Lieber, 2011; Csapo et al., 2020; Thorsteinsdóttir et al., 2011; Rayagiri et al., 2018), signaling (Chal and Pourquié, 2017), and transcription (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005; Buckingham and Relaix, 2015).
evidence: Pathway analysis identified enriched categories with citations.

claim: Both the upregulated and downregulated genes were significantly enriched for ECM genes, including distinct collagen gene isoforms.
source: Both the upregulated and downregulated genes were significantly enriched for ECM genes, including distinct collagen gene isoforms, with COL4A1, COL4A2, COL4A5, COL4A6, COL8A1, COL11A1, and COL13A1 UP in iMyoblasts compared to bMyoblasts, and COL6A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, COL1A2, COL5A2, COL7A1, COL8A2, and COL22A1 UP in bMyoblasts compared to iMyoblasts.
evidence: Pathway analysis showed enrichment of ECM genes with specific collagen isoforms.

claim: iMyoblasts and bMyoblasts differentially expressed members of matrix processing enzyme gene families, including MMP, ADAMTS, and ADAM, and members of matrix regulatory protein gene families ITG, KRT, CDH, SEMA, and LAM.
source: iMyoblasts and bMyoblasts also differentially expressed members of matrix processing enzyme gene families, including MMP, ADAMTS, and ADAM, and members of matrix regulatory protein gene families ITG, KRT, CDH, SEMA, and LAM, all of which have established regulatory functions during embryonic and adult myogenesis.
evidence: Pathway analysis showed differential expression of matrix-related genes.

claim: Signaling was among the top-ranked GO and KEGG categories and included receptor regulatory activity, receptor ligand activity, and signaling receptor activator activity (enriched among genes UP in bMyoblasts compared to iMyoblasts), and PI3K-Akt, MAPK, Rap1, and Ras pathways (enriched among genes UP in iMyoblasts vs. bMyoblasts).
source: Signaling was among the top-ranked GO and KEGG categories and included receptor regulatory activity, receptor ligand activity, and signaling receptor activator activity (enriched among genes UP in bMyoblasts compared to iMyoblasts), and PI3K-Akt, MAPK, Rap1, and Ras pathways (enriched among genes UP in iMyoblasts vs. bMyoblasts).
evidence: Pathway analysis identified enriched signaling categories.

claim: These pathways include differentially expressed FGF, WNT, and FZD gene family members.
source: These pathways include differentially expressed FGF, WNT, and FZD gene family members.
evidence: Pathway analysis identified specific gene families in signaling pathways.

claim: TGFB, PDGFA, EPHA2 and EPHB2, NOG, IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, and HMGA2 were UP in iMyoblasts.
source: Additionally, TGFB, PDGFA, EPHA2 and EPHB2, NOG, IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, and HMGA2 were UP in iMyoblasts, while GDNF, VEGFA, BMP4, BMP7, WISP1, SULF1, and GREM2 were UP in bMyoblasts.
evidence: Differential expression analysis identified specific genes upregulated in iMyoblasts.

claim: GDNF, VEGFA, BMP4, BMP7, WISP1, SULF1, and GREM2 were UP in bMyoblasts.
source: Additionally, TGFB, PDGFA, EPHA2 and EPHB2, NOG, IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, and HMGA2 were UP in iMyoblasts, while GDNF, VEGFA, BMP4, BMP7, WISP1, SULF1, and GREM2 were UP in bMyoblasts.
evidence: Differential expression analysis identified specific genes upregulated in bMyoblasts.

claim: Transcription categories included DNA-binding transcription activators, for which specific genes UP in bMyoblasts included KLF4, SOX8, SIX2, PITX3, SCX, SNAI1, SNAI2, and SMAD1, and genes UP in iMyoblasts included GATA3, GATA6, HAND2, MEIS2, GLI2, NOTCH1, ETS1, and ETS2.
source: Transcription categories included DNA-binding transcription activators, for which specific genes UP in bMyoblasts included KLF4, SOX8, SIX2, PITX3, SCX, SNAI1, SNAI2, and SMAD1, and genes UP in iMyoblasts included GATA3, GATA6, HAND2, MEIS2, GLI2, NOTCH1, ETS1, and ETS2.
evidence: Pathway analysis identified differentially expressed transcription factors.

claim: The top-ranked KEGG categories for genes UP in bMyoblasts compared to iMyoblasts included mineral absorption, complement and coagulation cascades, arachidonic acid metabolism, and retinoic acid metabolism.
source: The top-ranked KEGG categories for genes UP in bMyoblasts compared to iMyoblasts included mineral absorption, complement and coagulation cascades, arachidonic acid metabolism, and retinoic acid metabolism, whose functions in adult myogenesis are currently unknown.
evidence: Pathway analysis identified enriched KEGG categories.

claim: In all four pairwise comparisons between earlier stages (S1 or S2A) and committed iMyoblasts or bMyoblasts stages, genes UP in the committed myogenic stages are enriched for positive regulation of cell migration and TGFβ signaling.
source: In all four pairwise comparisons between earlier stages (S1 or S2A) and committed iMyoblasts or bMyoblasts stages, genes UP in the committed myogenic stages are enriched for positive regulation of cell migration and TGFβ signaling, while genes UP in the earlier stage are enriched in steroid and cholesterol biosynthesis categories, likely to inhibit replicative stress and replication check point activation leading to cell cycle arrest (Replogle et al., 2020).
evidence: Pathway analysis comparing developmental stages identified enriched categories with citation.

claim: Genes UP in the earlier stage are enriched in steroid and cholesterol biosynthesis categories, likely to inhibit replicative stress and replication check point activation leading to cell cycle arrest.
source: In all four pairwise comparisons between earlier stages (S1 or S2A) and committed iMyoblasts or bMyoblasts stages, genes UP in the committed myogenic stages are enriched for positive regulation of cell migration and TGFβ signaling, while genes UP in the earlier stage are enriched in steroid and cholesterol biosynthesis categories, likely to inhibit replicative stress and replication check point activation leading to cell cycle arrest (Replogle et al., 2020).
evidence: Pathway analysis identified enriched categories in earlier stages with citation and inference about function.

claim: These findings validate the identity of iMyoblasts as a bona fide PAX3/MYOD1 myogenic cell, distinct both from S1 and S2 cells at early developmental stages of iPSC induction and from adult PAX7/PAX3/MYF5/MYOD1 bMyoblasts.
source: These findings validate the identity of iMyoblasts as a bona fide PAX3/MYOD1 myogenic cell, distinct both from S1 and S2 cells at early developmental stages of iPSC induction and from adult PAX7/PAX3/MYF5/MYOD1 bMyoblasts.
evidence: The Results section summarizes the pathway analysis findings.

claim: The differentiation of Ctrl, FSHD1, and LGMDR7 iMyoblasts was compared in cultures using growth factor-free N2 medium to induce myotube differentiation.
source: The differentiation of Ctrl, FSHD1, and LGMDR7 iMyoblasts was compared in cultures using growth factor-free N2 medium to induce myotube differentiation.
evidence: The Results section describes the differentiation assay method.

claim: iMyotube cultures from these iMyoblasts upregulated CKM and MYH8 muscle genes with similar kinetics, as determined by qPCR assays.
source: iMyotube cultures from these iMyoblasts upregulated CKM and MYH8 muscle genes with similar kinetics, as determined by qPCR assays (Figure 4A).
evidence: qPCR data showed upregulation of muscle genes during differentiation.

claim: iMyotubes expressed low levels of adult MYH1 compared to bMyotubes, consistent with their identity as a fetal/embryonic lineage.
source: iMyotubes expressed low levels of adult MYH1 compared to bMyotubes (Figure 4A), consistent with their identity as a fetal/embryonic lineage.
evidence: qPCR data showed lower MYH1 expression in iMyotubes compared to bMyotubes.

claim: Ctrl and FSHD1 iMyotubes similarly upregulated the expression of muscle genes in both N2 and Opti-MEM growth factor-free media.
source: Ctrl and FSHD1 iMyotubes similarly upregulated the expression of muscle genes in both N2 and Opti-MEM growth factor-free media (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
